x: It seems that a strong posse of Australians will be crossing the Tasman to hit the New Zealand 10,000 metre Championship – including Marty Dent.

Australian Marty Dent had a cracking run in the 3000 metres Steeplechase - first man home after the Kenyan clean sweep – and in his fifth Commonwealth Games Mick Jones went over 70 metres in the hammer to place 5th.

Marty Dent, fresh from his great run in the Commonwealth Games steeplechase, writes from Australia and sends congratulations on a fifth consecutive SEAA 12-Stage win.

Marty Dent writes to let us know that he’s consolidating his form in Australia, running road and XC races in the Aussie winter: “I am hoping to be picked to run at the World Road Running champs in Hungary in October after I ran 62:57 for a half marathon last weekend.
Victorian Lee Troop was first across the line in 36:36 but 16 seconds later came Marty Dent in second spot with Erwin MacRae 4th and Adam Leane 30th.

And sure enough Marty Dent came out on top of the pile, winning his race in 8:04.59. Marty, who plans to attempt to qualify for next year’s World Championships in the 3000m Steeplechase was happy with his win.

Marty Dent, running for Australia, had also benefited from a conservative start and placed, 71st and fifth scorer for his team. Hats off to first Briton home Mo’ Farah who went through the field like a dose of salts from 68th on lap 1 to eventually place 10th.
